To soon issue draft framework for centralised assessment of CGST taxpayers: CBIC chief
 The new framework is likely to be implemented from next fiscal beginning April 1, 2027
 Updated - November 18, 2026 05:42 pm IST - New Delh 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs chairman Vivek Chaturvedi. File
 | Photo Credit: ANI
 The CBIC will soon release a draft framework for faceless and centralised assessment for 70 lakh taxpayers registered under the Central GST (CGST), a senior official said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
 The new framework is likely to be implemented from next fiscal beginning April 1, 2027.
 Six key GST officials in Chennai transferred after Sowcarpet traders incident Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) chairman Vivek Chaturvedi said the CGST-registered taxpayers fall broadly in two categories -- large ones with multiple GSTINs within a state or GSTINs spread across various states, and small entrepreneurs registered in a particular geography.
 "We (CBIC) are weaving our thoughts around the two concepts of a faceless and a centralised administration for the CGST taxpayers. And we have created a framework. The framework should be out for public consultation and stakeholder consultation very shortly," Mr. Chaturvedi said at a PHDCCI event.
 Mr. Chaturvedi said the Central government intends to bring a new paradigm of administration for CGST taxpayers.
 "It will both be a centralised administration where the large taxpayer can walk into the physical office and all their needs, including registration, written scrutiny, adjudication, reviews, and appeals, are taken care of in one geography. For the rest of the taxpayers, we intend to bring in a faceless assistance system," Mr. Chaturvedi said.
 Finance Ministry notifies new Central GST tax rates The CBIC chief asked the industry chambers and stakeholders to send their views once the framework is out for public consultation.
 Of the 70 lakh CGST-registered taxpayers, about 2 lakh are registered with multiple CGST jurisdiction either in one state or across different states.
 After the 57th GST Council meeting on October 8, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had said that the framework for faceless assessment for CGST taxpayers will be put up for consultation and will be implemented from fiscal year 2027-28.
 Under the proposed framework, tax notices, hearings and orders would be dealt with on a national platform rather than individual formations.
 A taxpayer registered under CGST operating in several states would then deal with one system instead of several offices.
 GST procedure simplified after recent reforms by government of India: CGST Joint Commissioner Under the Goods and Services Tax (GST), taxpayers have been divided between CGST and SGST officers based on a formula decided by the GST Council to ensure a single interface.
 All administrative control over 90% of taxpayers having turnover below ₹1.5 crore vests with state tax administration. The remaining 10 per cent is with central tax administration.
 Taxpayers with a turnover above ₹1.5 crore are divided equally between Central and state tax administration.
 The GST Council has decided to scrap the arrest powers of tax officers which Chaturvedi described as a "historic step". The Council last month also hiked the threshold for launching prosecution for GST offences to ₹5 crore.
 "The message is that the tax administration must be an economic partnership, and not an exercise in coercion," he said.
 Mr. Chaturvedi further said that the Council's decision that GST officers will be allowed to stop vehicles carrying high-value goods for inspection only at their origin and destination states after prior authorisation from a senior officer will bring competitive advantage for businesses.
 Before this, GST officers could stop vehicles in transit irrespective of jurisdiction and ask for documents.
 Next-Gen GST and India’s next phase of growth "Our transporters, our manufacturers and our exporters will now move goods nationwide with far fewer stoppages than what was the current practise," he said.
 Under the GST, an e-way bill is mandatory for transiting goods valued at ₹50,000 and above, both inter- and intra-states.
 The GST Council meeting in October also approved that only the state in which the goods started (source state) and the destination state may inspect the goods moving in a conveyance. States along the route will not be able to stop the conveyance.
